facts.text: Amlodipine besylate tablets are contraindicated in patients with known sensitivity to amlodipine.
Symptomatic hypotension may occur, particularly in patients with severe aortic stenosis; acute hypotension is unlikely due to the drug’s gradual onset.
Worsening angina and acute myocardial infarction can develop after initiating or increasing the dose of amlodipine, especially in patients with severe obstructive coronary artery disease.
facts.population: Patients with severe obstructive coronary artery disease

facts.text: Because amlodipine is extensively metabolized by the liver and its half‑life is prolonged in hepatic impairment, titrate slowly in patients with severe hepatic impairment.
Adult recommended starting dose is 5 mg once daily; maximum dose is 10 mg once daily. Small, fragile, elderly patients or those with hepatic insufficiency may start at 2.5 mg once daily.
When titrating, wait 7–14 days between dose adjustments; more rapid titration is permissible if the patient is closely monitored.
For chronic stable or vasospastic angina, the dose range is 5–10 mg once daily; a lower dose is suggested for elderly or hepatic‑insufficient patients, with most requiring 10 mg for adequate effect.
For coronary artery disease, the recommended dose is 5–10 mg once daily; the majority of patients required 10 mg in clinical studies.
Pediatric patients (ages 6–17 years) receive 2.5–5 mg once daily for hypertension; doses >5 mg daily have not been studied in this population.
Elderly patients (≥65 years) have a 40–60 % increase in AUC due to decreased clearance; start at the low end of the dosing range and adjust cautiously.
Co‑administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases amlodipine exposure; consider dose reduction and monitor for hypotension and edema.
CYP3A inducers may reduce amlodipine efficacy; blood pressure should be closely monitored when co‑administered.
When combined with sildenafil, monitor for hypotension.
Amlodipine increases systemic exposure of simvastatin; limit simvastatin dose to ≤20 mg daily.
Amlodipine may increase exposure of cyclosporine or tacrolimus; monitor trough levels and adjust immunosuppressant doses as needed.
